name: Unwound
label: Kill Rock Stars
lede: Three kids from Tumwater who covered Hüsker Dü, a drummer who took over in 1992, and a run of records that got stranger with every one.

eras.title: Giant Henry, high school, and a new name
eras.text: Three Tumwater high schoolers started as a cover band and ended up in Olympia, the town of Bikini Kill and the Kill Rock Stars label. By the end of 1992 they were Unwound, with the drummer who defined their sound.

years.h: [[Justin Trosper|95ea55c8-ecc7-4948-9d57-c621fd26f1e1]], [[Vern Rumsey|a4d62ca9-11fa-4658-90a7-71317f8f37d0]] and [[Brandt Sandeno|690ab2ad-94df-4fbc-bf61-e93b9076bc42]] form Giant Henry
years.p: Three Tumwater high school students start a band that covers Redd Kross, SNFU and Hüsker Dü. Johnny Wilson briefly drums, and the Melvins push them toward something slower and heavier.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, the band spent its first years playing covers before finding its own sound. Later reissues of the Giant Henry material by the Numero Group show how much of Unwound was already there.

years.h: Giant Henry play their last show, then become Unwound
years.p: After a self-titled demo as Cygnus X-1, the band settles on the name Unwound. A record made in early 1992 sits on the shelf until it comes out as Unwound on Honey Bear in 1995.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the last Giant Henry show to June 1, 1991. The Numero Group later released the pre-Unwound recordings as Big Baby on Record Store Day 2013.

years.h: [[Sara Lund|82a0bf96-2d58-40a2-8323-be8e08513a7b]] takes over the drum stool from Brandt Sandeno
years.p: Lund, who had been playing in a band called Witchypoo, replaces Sandeno in July 1992. She, Trosper and Rumsey stay a trio for the next decade.
years.xp: Lund taught herself to play, and her drumming gave the band the loose, pushing pulse that became its signature. Sandeno left the band but not the story: he later played on the last record and joined Trosper in [[Survival Knife|e773449a-49e5-4eab-b765-a9d45ec0cdb6]].

eras.title: Kill Rock Stars, Steve Fisk and three records in three years
eras.text: Slim Moon heard them live and gave the label its first record that wasn't spoken word. With producer Steve Fisk at Seattle's Avast! and John and Stu's, Unwound put out an album a year.

years.h: [[Slim Moon|602432a1-35ce-40ef-90e8-c4a123d438bf]] sees Unwound live and decides to put out their album
years.p: The Kill Rock Stars founder attends a show and signs on to release what becomes Fake Train. Moon also works as an assistant engineer on the sessions.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, Moon was won over by seeing the band play. Fake Train was recorded over two weekends in February and March 1993 at Avast! in Seattle, with [[Steve Fisk|c851ef86-5278-4537-8b51-7ccedb4ae903]] producing and Tim Green and Stuart Hallerman engineering.

years.h: Fake Train: the first music record on Kill Rock Stars
years.p: Everything Kill Rock Stars had released before it was spoken word. The working title was Rat Conspiracy, and the cover is a vandalized copy of Tom Jones's Tom that Trosper owned.
years.xp: Sara Lund later said she was unhappy with her own performance on the record; critics disagreed. The Rat Conspiracy name came back for the 2014 Numero Group box set.

years.cap: Original Unwound members Justin Trosper & Sara Lund performing at the Numero ... · Wikimedia
years.h: Late-night sessions at Avast! in Seattle for the second album
years.p: From late November to mid-December 1993 the band records with Steve Fisk at Avast!. They come out with shorter songs, odd time signatures and more melody than the debut.
years.xp: People assumed the title New Plastic Ideas referred to Mondrian. Trosper said he made it up on the spot.

years.h: New Plastic Ideas, with cover art from a classical LP
years.p: Kill Rock Stars issues the second album on CD, vinyl and cassette. The Vinyl Factory later described it as a step away from the feedback-heavy sound of Fake Train.
years.xp: Reviews were mixed at first: Select called it dense and angry. Pitchfork later heard a huge leap in articulation. Wikipedia gives March 21 and Discogs-based lists give March 18, so this page says March.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Future of What · KEXP
years.h: The Future of What, recorded in December at John and Stu's
years.p: Steve Fisk produces the third album in Seattle. The cover uses a design by Soviet constructivist Yakov Chernikhov, and the band was listening to Wire, Fire Engines, krautrock and Stereolab.

years.h: The 1992 recording finally comes out as Unwound on Honey Bear
years.p: The self-titled record made in early 1992, with Brandt Sandeno on drums, is released three years late by Honey Bear Records.

eras.title: Synths, saxophone, and two weeks in a studio
eras.text: The band leaned into the studio: keyboards on Repetition, a sax on Challenge for a Civilized Society, a session for John Peel, and a first trip overseas to sell it.

years.h: Repetition: synths arrive, and it becomes their best seller
years.p: Recorded in January 1996 with Fisk and John Goodmanson, it is the band's first studio-minded record. KEXP calls it their best seller from the original run, with "Message Received" and "Corpse Pose" its best-known songs.
years.xp: "Corpse Pose" came out as a single in March 1996. Trosper said he liked the word Repetition because it describes a lot of things.

years.h: Matador collects singles on Further Listening
years.p: The indie label Matador puts out a singles compilation, Further Listening, in May 1996.

years.h: The Light at the End of the Tunnel Is a Train EP arrives
years.p: Kill Rock Stars releases this EP in 1997, between Repetition and Challenge for a Civilized Society.

years.src: Wikipedia: Challenge for a Civilized Society · KEXP
years.h: Challenge for a Civilized Society: eighteen months of nothing, then two weeks
years.p: After an 18-month gap, the band writes in about a month and records August 1 to 15, 1997 with Fisk. It spends 16 weeks on the CMJ Radio 200 and peaks at number four.
years.xp: Trosper felt the songs were tighter but the album less inspired than the others. He credited Fisk for trying production ideas most producers wouldn't. Wikipedia says fans and band alike consider it the least successful.

years.cap: Unwound on the road in Europe (photo TBD)
years.h: A BBC session for John Peel, and a bootleg that keeps it alive
years.p: Unwound record a session for John Peel at the BBC in 1998. It circulates as the bootleg Live in London on Love Letter and gets an official release as the Peel Sessions EP in 2015.
years.xp: The Numero Group also released a show from June 30, 1999 in Reykjavik, Iceland, as 06/30/1999: Reykjavik, Iceland in 2014. Wikipedia calls Primavera 2023 their first European show since 1999.

years.h: A Single History: 1991–1997 collects the singles
years.p: Kill Rock Stars rounds up the band's early singles. According to KEXP, the title track uses parts of Challenge for a Civilized Society played backward.

eras.title: The last statement
eras.text: Unwound built their own studio in Olympia and made a double album that finally sounded like the band inside Trosper's head. They toured it with two extra players, and did not last much beyond the tour.

q: a record that could stand as a final statement
years.src: Wikipedia: Leaves Turn Inside You · KEXP · Vice
years.h: Leaves Turn Inside You: a double album in their own studio
years.p: Self-produced in Olympia after years with Steve Fisk, the record uses Mellotron and ARP synths and brings Brandt Sandeno back on keyboards. Pitchfork gave it a 9.0.
years.xp: Trosper cited Bowie's Low, Radiohead's Kid A and the Flaming Lips' The Soft Bulletin. He said it was a record that could stand as a final statement. Sources differ on the studio: KEXP calls it a farmhouse, Wikipedia names it MagRecOne, Vice a basement with an eight-track.

years.h: A 37-date tour as a five-piece, cut short by September 11
years.p: Unwound take Sandeno on keys, guitarist David Scott Stone and soundman Dave Doughman on the road. The attacks cancel their biggest shows in Boston and New York City.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, the expanded lineup was under-rehearsed and early shows suffered. Rumsey broke his hands punching a wall after a San Diego show and kept playing in pain. A bootlegger, Mike Ziegler, recorded the whole tour, and Lund and Trosper later used his tapes to build Live Leaves.

q: it was an unchecked serious drinking problem
years.h: Unwound end it on April Fool's Day
years.p: Shortly after co-headlining All Tomorrow's Parties, the band announces it is done. An early T-shirt had read "Unwound 1991–2091".
years.xp: Sara Lund told Stereogum the cause was drinking that had gone unchecked and that everyone shared blame. Wikipedia adds that after the tour Rumsey suggested Unwound become a studio-only band, and that Trosper and Lund declined. Rumsey became a father, and Trosper stayed largely out of music for nearly a decade.

eras.title: The archive opens
eras.text: For a decade the band was mostly a rumor. Then a live album, an online archive and a Chicago label's box sets turned Unwound into a catalog people could finally own.

years.h: Survival Knife and other next bands
years.p: [[Justin Trosper|95ea55c8-ecc7-4948-9d57-c621fd26f1e1]] and [[Brandt Sandeno|690ab2ad-94df-4fbc-bf61-e93b9076bc42]] start [[Survival Knife|e773449a-49e5-4eab-b765-a9d45ec0cdb6]]. [[Sara Lund|82a0bf96-2d58-40a2-8323-be8e08513a7b]] plays in Hungry Ghost and the Corin Tucker Band, and Vern Rumsey forms Flora v. Fauna and works as an engineer, including for [[Blonde Redhead|6821bf3f-5d5b-4b0f-8fa4-79d2ab2d9219]].
years.xp: Wikipedia says that in 2011 Lund, Trosper and Rumsey met to discuss the live album and seriously considered reforming, and dropped the idea when Rumsey was still drinking despite court-ordered AA meetings.

years.h: Live Leaves and the Unwound Archive appear
years.p: Ten years after the split, the band releases Live Leaves, drawn from the 2001 tour tapes. Around the same time it launches unwoundarchive.com, full of flyers, photos, video and tour history.
years.xp: Lund and Trosper listened to every recorded show and charted the best versions of each song. The archive runs from Giant Henry to the last tour.

years.h: The Numero Group licenses the catalog, and Giant Henry's Big Baby lands
years.p: In 2013 the band licenses its back catalog to the Chicago label Numero Group. The first release is Big Baby, the 1991 Giant Henry recordings, for Record Store Day.

years.h: Rat Conspiracy: Fake Train and New Plastic Ideas in one box
years.p: The second Numero Group box set pairs the first two Kill Rock Stars albums with a disc of live tracks, singles and demos. Pitchfork gave it a 9.1.

years.h: Numero finishes the box sets: No Energy, Empire, What Was Wound
years.p: After Kid Is Gone in 2013 and Rat Conspiracy in 2014, Numero adds No Energy (October 2014), Empire (September 2015) and What Was Wound (December 2016).

eras.title: Bass for Vern
eras.text: Vern Rumsey's death in 2020 closed the door on the original trio. Two years later Trosper and Lund announced shows in his memory, with Jared Warren on bass.

years.src: Brooklyn Vegan · Wikipedia: Unwound · Wikipedia: Vern Rumsey
years.h: Vern Rumsey dies at 47
years.p: The Unwound co-founder dies on August 6, 2020. The reports I found do not state a cause.
years.xp:
Numero Group's Ken Shipley said his death was a reminder that an era had ended, and that he had known for some time Rumsey was not well. According to Wikipedia, Rumsey went through a health crisis and rehab in 2017-18 and relapsed afterward; in April 2019 he was unable to play at a rehearsal and gave Trosper and Lund his blessing to play shows without him.

Wikipedia says [[Jared Warren|0bc59e8e-4911-4f0f-b851-3a638af30235]] (Big Business, formerly Karp) rehearsed with them in March 2020, before the pandemic ended those talks.

years.h: Unwound announce reunion shows in Rumsey's memory
years.p: Trosper and Lund say they will tour in early 2023 with Jared Warren on bass and Scott Seckington on guitar. In 2013 Trosper had told Vice a reunion was a 90 percent chance of not happening.

years.cap: First show in 21 years, Astoria, Oregon (photo TBD)
years.h: First show in 21 years: a surprise gig at a dance center in Astoria
years.p: About 200 ticket holders see Unwound at the Astoria Arts and Movement Center in Oregon, asked to leave their phones in their pockets. Brandt Sandeno, Doug Martsch and Liz Harris of Grouper travel to see it.
years.xp: Paste noted Warren's bass was tidier than Rumsey's fluid style, which left room for more layered guitars. The official tour started February 3 in Seattle.

years.h: Three nights at Irving Plaza, then Primavera in Barcelona
years.p: The reunion tour covers the U.S., including three sold-out nights at Irving Plaza in New York City, and reaches Primavera Sound in Barcelona on June 2, 2023.
